quest.title: Fortress of Meropide
quest.description: At Neuvillette's behest, you are sent to Fortress of Meropide on trumped-up charges to secretly investigate. Your life behind bars is about to begin...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x875, Mora x38100, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x7

chapter.title: To the Stars Shining in the Depths

talks.objective: Follow Deakin

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So... are you one of the guards here? Is there anything we should be careful of while we're here?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... did Paimon already ask something she wasn't supposed to?

dialogues.speaker: Deakin
dialogues.text: Why should I tell you anything? What's in it for me?

choices.text: You sure don't seem like a guard.

response.speaker: Deakin
response.text: *sigh* This is exactly why I can't stand new fish. I wouldn't even be doing this if it weren't for the Credit Coupons.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Credit Coupons?

response.speaker: Deakin
response.text: Alright, seeing as you're not the annoying kind that's getting dragged in here crying and blubbering, I guess I can tell you a few things... But next time, it'll cost you some coupons.

response.speaker: Deakin
response.text: Mora means nothing here. Here, we use Credit Coupons.

response.speaker: Deakin
response.text: Coupons can get you almost anything in the Fortress of Meropide. Desires? Fulfilled. You want power? No problem. Coupons can even change fate itself.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So Credit Coupons are a currency that can only be used here?

response.speaker: Deakin
response.text: It's not as simple as that. Like Marette said, everyone gets a chance at "rebirth."

response.speaker: Deakin
response.text: No matter how much money or power you had before, it means nothing once you set foot inside the Fortress of Meropide. You have to start over and earn your coupons.

response.speaker: Deakin
response.text: Everyone starts from the same place, and you have a chance at a new, less terrible life...

response.speaker: Deakin
response.text: I guess that's the real purpose of the coupons. They symbolize true fairness and true justice!

response.speaker: Deakin
response.text: And this is also exactly why so many criminals choose not to return to the outside world even after they've served their sentence.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, so that's what the Fortress of Meropide is like... Paimon was under the impression that it'd be more like a prison...

response.speaker: Deakin
response.text: It certainly ain't all sunshine and roses here, but it's also not the worst place to be... You'd better take a good look at the scenery now, it'll be the last chance you get for a while.

response.speaker: Deakin
response.text: After being away from the sunlight for so long, even the terrifying depths of the sea start to feel like home... it just stops feeling oppressive, you know?

response.speaker: Deakin
response.text: Oh, I'm actually an inmate like you two. Welcoming newcomers is a job I've picked up to earn some extra coupons.

choices.text: Have you ever seen the Duke?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh? Why aren't you answering us again?

response.speaker: Deakin
response.text: I've told you enough for free. Any more info is gonna cost ya.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So all you care about is Mora... Wait, no, coupons!?

response.speaker: Deakin
response.text: Almost there, it's down through here. Your turn to give it a try.

choices.text: Have you seen a Harbinger from Snezhnaya?
Why were you sent to bring us in?

talks.objective: Ride the lift
Go to the corners of the corridors

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It was okay. His attitude could use some work, though.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: I see. In that case, I regret to announce that Deakin here has just missed the best opportunity in his prison career to be promoted.

dialogues.speaker: Deakin
dialogues.text: I... uh, I admit that I was only thinking about the coupons... I'm sorry to have disappointed you, Your Grace. I originally... I once hoped for a chance to do some higher-level work.

dialogues.speaker: Deakin
dialogues.text: *sigh* I had no idea you two were big shots who were worthy of speaking with His Grace... Losing out on such a big opportunity because I couldn't see past my own nose...

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Plenty of time ahead, Deakin. There will be more opportunities.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Well, I believe that concludes the introductions. We've already taken enough time here. Deakin, if you would.

dialogues.speaker: Deakin
dialogues.text: Yes! Your Grace, I'll take my leave now!

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Please, follow me. To make you feel more welcome, I'll show you around the various facilities of the Fortress of Meropide. I hope it will help you adjust to life here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: He's going to personally give us a tour? Paimon can't figure out what this guy's thinking at all...

choices.text: Let's just roll with it for now.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No wonder Charlotte's so interested in him! He's one of those mysterious types. Alright, let's keep up with him.

choices.text: But I hope he doesn't know too much already.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: He's taken great care of us. Splendid chap, really.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Outstanding. Well, Deakin, I recall we discussed fate during our last work meeting. I believe that fate will reward all those who take every aspect of their work and life seriously.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: When you return to your bunk, you'll find the guards have issued some extra Credit Coupons to you.

dialogues.speaker: Deakin
dialogues.text: Oh, thank you... Thank you, Your Grace! Oh, and you two! I can't believe you gave me such praise. If you need anything in the future, anything, please come find me anytime! No Credit Coupons necessary!

talks.objective: Talk to Wriothesley at the Coupon Cafeteria

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: There's no need to be so reserved. The label of criminal is nothing but one of many identities, and being criminally inclined here at the Fortress is just one of many ways to survive.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is it really okay for the warden to think like that? We're real criminals, you know! What if we're too difficult to handle?

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Well then, maybe you'll be able to carve out a name and a place for yourselves in this underwater world, hm?

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: But before you go in swinging, please remember that in the Fortress of Meropide, it's better to not cause trouble for yourself... or for the guards.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Now, we've arrived at a very important place: the Coupon Cafeteria. You can come here and claim one welfare meal each day.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Welfare meal? You mean... it doesn't cost anything?

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: That's right. Criminals are essential to fortress operations, so we must guarantee that they at least have the basic means to survive.

dialogues.speaker: Wolsey
dialogues.text: Haha, but that's not how it was! Back in the day, it'd cost you Credit Coupons just to get a cup of water here.

dialogues.speaker: Wolsey
dialogues.text: For fish like you who'd just arrived with nothing, you'd have to go to work hungry until you earned enough coupons to eat.

dialogues.speaker: Wolsey
dialogues.text: It was only after His Grace became the administrator that we got the free meal rule.

dialogues.speaker: Wolsey
dialogues.text: Now everyone gets a square meal every day, even no-good slackers who've never picked up a wrench in their whole lives. Nobody starves to death here.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: In the Fortress of Meropide, Credit Coupons are the only currency, and everything must be purchased. In some sense, you could say using the coupons is a form of trade.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: But trade is always conducted by people, so if we want trade here to prosper, we need everyone to work hard and live their lives.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: If nobody could even afford a meal, then the whole fortress would be up in arms. That would only make things more difficult for me.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: So rather than saying that we're giving everyone a free meal here, you should say that everyone's hard work has improved the living conditions in the Fortress of Meropide.

dialogues.speaker: Wolsey
dialogues.text: Your Grace's reasoning is correct, but what I said is also true.

dialogues.speaker: Wolsey
dialogues.text: Whatever the case, hard work is rewarded here. You'd be hard-pressed to find anywhere else as fair and reasonable.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Right, Paimon sees your point. By that logic, this place doesn't seem so bad after all.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, no! We shouldn't drop our guard so quickly... But it seems the inmates really respect the Duke because of his attitude, right? Hmm, we should still try to verify the truth with our own eyes.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Let's continue, this way.

talks.objective: Talk to Wriothesley at the Pankration Ring

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: This place is known as the "Pankration Ring."

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Sometimes we have criminals who have more energy than they know what to do with... their daily work alone isn't enough of an outlet for them.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: So, instead of leaving them to their own devices, we've provided them with this dedicated venue. This way, nobody will get involved unless they want to be.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Pankration matches... And you can earn extra coupons! What do you think, {NICKNAME}? Interested?

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: But I must warn you that your sentence will be extended if you fail to restrain yourself and end up seriously injuring or killing your opponent.

choices.text: In that case, I'll pass...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So, did you set this place up too?

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: No, actually. I just granted approval for the organizer to use this area to build the ring, and I collect a portion of the proceeds in return.

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: Of course, the fees are also quite useful.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh... Do you mind if we ask what they're used for?

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: Sure. Ensuring personal safety, maintaining the arena, and resolving any conflicts that arise... Why? Are you interested in how to manage a Pankration Ring?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, no no! Paimon was just wondering if that's how you paid for everyone's welfare meals...

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: A reasonable guess. I see you have a talent for entrepreneurship.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You hear that? Paimon has a talent! So, we can start a business here?

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: That is something you can discuss between yourselves later. Let's move on for now.

choices.text: Seems you know me too well.

talks.objective: Talk to Wriothesley at the dormitories

dialogues.speaker: Fitzroy
dialogues.text: Ah, Y—Your Grace! Good morning... I mean, good afternoon! ...No wait, what time is it again?

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: What time indeed. Time waits for no one, so it's best to keep an eye on it.

dialogues.speaker: Fitzroy
dialogues.text: Ah, m—my apologies, Your Grace! *panting*

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Geez, that guy's so nervous he almost forgot to breathe...

dialogues.speaker: Fitzroy
dialogues.text: *deep breath* Sorry, forgive my manners...

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: These are the dormitories, which is where inmates sleep. The guards will inform you where your bunk is later.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: In the Fortress of Meropide, criminals usually spend most of their time in either the production zone or the sleeping areas.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The production zone... what does it produce? Is that where we'll be working?

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Not necessarily. Though working in the production zone is the most reliable way to earn Credit Coupons, if you have other skills, you can skip your shifts to earn them in other ways.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow... Wait, you're the manager of this place and you're just telling us to our faces that it's okay to skip work!?

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: The fact that the Fortress of Meropide has continued operating completely autonomously is proof enough that most people are willing to work honestly and earn a stable income.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: As for what we produce... many of the clockwork machines seen all over Fontaine originate from our workshop.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Therefore, the Fortress of Meropide is not only a place where criminals serve their sentences, but also a giant machine factory.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: There's no need for me to get into specifics about the production process now. You'll experience it all firsthand when you report for work tomorrow.

choices.text: Thank you, Your Grace!

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: Let's move on. The tour continues over this way.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: O—Oh...

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Oh! You really scared me there... I didn't expect to see you here, Your Grace. I thought maybe I was so tired from work that I was starting to see things.

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: The only thing you should be seeing is the work in front of you. Stay focused and keep up the pace.

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: Oh? Is something the matter?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehehe, it's nothing... Paimon's just worried about how hard we'll have to work tomorrow, hehe...

choices.text: You got it, Boss!

talks.objective: Go to the infirmary and talk to Wriothesley

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Your Grace? What are you doing in the infirmary at a time like this? Oh no, you didn't injure yourself, did you?

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Not yet, unfortunately for you. But thank you for your concern, Sigewinne.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Hehe, then you must be here for those two.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Allow me to introduce you. This is the infirmary, and Sigewinne here is the Fortress of Meropide's head nurse.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Hello, new faces! They call me the head nurse, but I actually handle all the nurse-related work all by myself down here!

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Since you seem to have some rare downtime with no patients, perhaps you could find the time to join us for dinner?

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Oooh, then these two must be some important convicts. Sure, I'll join the welcome party!

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Thank you. Your presence will be the piece de resistance for today's tour.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, so the tour part is over now?

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: I believe I've already covered the primary aspects of life here in the fortress. As for your work, there'll be someone else to guide you through the details. Hmm, is there anything else...?

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: I seldom conduct tours, so why don't you just ask if you have any questions?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, uh, well... This is our first time here, Paimon's not sure what to ask...

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Then let's head back to the Coupon Cafeteria. Maybe a meal will help you think up some questions.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: You should at least try to be excited. Our free meals are actually pretty good here.

talks.objective: Go to the Coupon Cafeteria to get some food

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: What do you think of the food? Does it meet your expectations?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, it looks delicious... Neuvillette made it sound like living conditions in the Fortress of Meropide weren't very good. Who woulda guessed that criminals get to eat tasty food like this every day!

choices.text: The main thing is that it's free.

response.speaker: Sigewinne
response.text: Isn't that the meal box that only super lucky people manage to draw? Seems like you two are quite fortunate.

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: It actually has nothing to do with luck in this case. I had a word with Wolsey so you didn't have to draw lots like everyone else.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, you mean the meals are random?

response.speaker: Sigewinne
response.text: Yes, what you get to eat depends completely on your luck. You could say that it's a... distasteful little game that Chef Wolsey likes to play here in the cafeteria.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon knew it! If criminals got to eat tasty food like this every meal, the crime rate in Fontaine would skyrocket for sure!

response.speaker: Sigewinne
response.text: Excuse me, did I hear you mention Neuvillette just now? I've been wondering how he's doing. Is he busy with work? Has he been taking care of his health?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: He seems healthy no matter how you look at him, but he works so hard all the time, so it must be really tiring...

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: Sounds like he hasn't changed a bit. Looks like you can stop worrying so much, Sigewinne.

response.speaker: Sigewinne
response.text: That's good... but I still feel like it's been too long since I've heard any news about him.

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: No news is good news.

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: Maybe the next time I've got something to discuss with him, I can invite you to accompany us.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm? But isn't the Fortress of Meropide independent from Fontaine's court system? What do you two have to discuss?

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: Well, we provide all kinds of mechanical products for official use, and some essential goods have to be obtained from the overworld, so we naturally have to stay in touch about this and that.

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: Monsieur Neuvillette's character is unimpeachable. No matter the question, you can discuss it openly and freely with him. Talking with him feels quite effortless.

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: In light of that, I am quite willing to go out of my way to show respect and accommodate him.

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: In fact, right now I'm treating you two as guests invited by Monsieur Neuvillette, but unfortunately, I can only do so until the end of this meal.

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: After this, you two will just be inmates here.

choices.text: Understood.

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: You're very welcome. Well, your new life awaits.

choices.text: Thank you for your hospitality.
Mine's pretty good, too.

talks.objective: Return to the dormitories and talk to Fielding

dialogues.speaker: Fielding
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME} and Paimon, right? Listen up. As new inmates, the only thing you need to worry about is what to do and when to do it. Don't make any extra trouble for yourself.

dialogues.speaker: Fielding
dialogues.text: Your bunks are right over there. Follow me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whew, so this is where we'll be sleeping from now on...? Paimon can't believe this! *sigh* The days of staying home and reading detective stories are like a dream now...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #By the way, {NICKNAME}, we saw a lot of things worth investigating just now...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Even though the Duke didn't say it too directly, judging from what he said at the end, it seems that he was only welcoming because we know Neuvillette...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We are criminals, and Paimon did eat that cake... But we're actually here to help Neuvillette.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... Is it possible that he knows we're here on a mission? Or is Paimon overthinking things?

choices.text: It's very possible...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, Paimon thinks so, too. He probably knew why we came here from the very beginning and intentionally wanted to send us a message...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Maybe something like, "Hey, I have my eyes on you, so don't try anything funny!"

choices.text: But there's nothing we can do about that.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, you're right. It's not like we can go back to Neuvillette empty-handed and say, "The Duke looked scary, so we gave up."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... And besides, the Duke said that he was willing to go out of his way to show his respect for Neuvillette, right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So we at least need to try! But Paimon hasn't got a clue where we should start our investigation...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: There was one other important thing...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You mean...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Lyney's presence here.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! That's what Paimon was thinking, too! Paimon almost spilled the beans when we ran into him.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Fortunately, based on his attitude, it looks like the Duke sees Lyney as just another inmate.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We worked so hard to help clear Lyney and Lynette's names, and yet we turn around and bam! He's in prison anyway?

choices.text: If I had to guess...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, right! Lyney and Lynette are from the House of the Hearth! They work for The Knave, so they could be here to investigate, too!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: And look, there's something over there...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Oh, it's a card! Paimon didn't notice it earlier...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It looks like a magician's prop, Lyney must have left it here! He's in prison and still doing his little tricks, huh... Let Paimon have a look!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It was nice to bump into you again. Let's catch up in the production zone tomorrow.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What in the world? It's written like he's greeting a buddy on the street... Paimon thought he'd write something important.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: This proves that he's up to something here, too.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If you say so... We can ask him what's going on tomorrow. Let's get some rest now.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: With a bit of trepidation, you and Paimon spend your first night in the Fortress of Meropide...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, you're finally awake.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You're up early today, Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, it's Paimon's first day as a prisoner... Last night Paimon dreamed about getting interrogated by the guards until Paimon told them everything, and then Paimon woke up...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You told them everything?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, c'mon! It's just a dream, okay? Paimon wouldn't really squeal... maybe...

response.speaker: Fielding
response.text: Hey, lazybones! What're you still doing here? If you don't want to starve, then get yourselves over to the production zone!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah! Sorry, we're going right away!

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You set off as soon as possible after asking Fielding about the location of the Production Zone.

choices.text: I'd say he's here for the same reason we are.
We're already here, after all.
He probably knows more than he's letting on.

talks.objective: Go to the production zone to talk to Grainville

dialogues.speaker: Grainville
dialogues.text: Ah, you must be the catch of the day. Looks like you've got some luck, getting assigned this space...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yep, we just arrived yesterday and...

dialogues.speaker: Grainville
dialogues.text: Don't interrupt me when I'm speaking!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yessir!

dialogues.speaker: Grainville
dialogues.text: Listen carefully to my instructions. I don't want any mishaps. Every machine here is worth more than the both of you!

dialogues.speaker: Grainville
dialogues.text: Working around these machines can be very dangerous. Do your job well, and you can eat in the cafeteria after your shift. Get sloppy, and you dine in the infirmary.

dialogues.speaker: Grainville
dialogues.text: Anyway, the Fortress of Meropide doesn't want to lose a single one of its machines, and it also doesn't want to waste the production potential of any inmate. You got that?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Got it!

dialogues.speaker: Grainville
dialogues.text: Your job is to use the machine over there to process widgets.

dialogues.speaker: Grainville
dialogues.text: Watch carefully and make sure you step on the pedal at the right time. If the machine gets jammed, then give it a little "maintenance" with your fist.

dialogues.speaker: Grainville
dialogues.text: Here, take this.

dialogues.speaker: Grainville
dialogues.text: Bring me the processed widgets and I'll give you some Credit Coupons in exchange.

talks.objective: Process widget
Take the widget

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Are you finished eating? Then I recommend that you return to the dormitories and rest. You have work to do tomorrow.

dialogues.speaker: Wriothesley
dialogues.text: Perhaps you were hoping to ask for some special privileges? Sorry, you'll have to use Credit Coupons like everyone else. It's not as comfy here as you might imagine.

talks.objective: Give the products to Grainville

dialogues.speaker: Grainville
dialogues.text: Hmm, this one is... tolerable... though since the processing is done by machine, the product is all pretty much the same anyway.

dialogues.speaker: Grainville
dialogues.text: Alright, I'll pass you for now, and we'll count up how many Credit Coupons you've earned.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whew, Paimon's exhausted! We're done now, right? Oh, that foreman! He's so scary that Paimon couldn't even speak...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh... even though Paimon's starving and wants to head straight to the Coupon Cafeteria... we still need to meet Lyney first, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: He probably just finished up his work too, he should be around here somewhere...

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: Now that I've gotten a good look at you two, I think you're very cute.

dialogues.speaker: Sigewinne
dialogues.text: After all, heavy is the head that wears the cutesie crown. I guess I just want to say, just take care of yourself and don't get hurt.

talks.objective: Keep looking for Lyney in the area
Keep looking for Lyney
Keep looking for Lyney

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Hey! Over here!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wha—! You scared Paimon! How did you appear out of nowhere like that!?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Oh? You scare so easily now? Is there something worrying you these days?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You little... The only thing we were worried about was trying to find you!

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Hehe, sorry, sorry! Come over here, and keep it down...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, Lynette! You're here too! You two really are inseparable.

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: That's right, my brother simply can't stand to be away from me.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Uh, it's not just Lynette, Freminet is also here. Do you still remember him?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, you mean that diver from the House of the Hearth, right? Paimon remembers seeing him in the Court of Fontaine before.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Now hurry up and tell us, how did you end up as criminals this time? We fought so hard at court to prove you were innocent, but now it looks like our incredible court battle was for nothing!

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Sadly, even the tiniest of things can land you in prison these days, you know. I put together a street performance and used the popularity we gained from the opera house incident to attract a big crowd.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And then...?

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: Next, I invited several audience members to participate in the show. And then, with the entire audience watching... their wallets suddenly disappeared!

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: My brother was charged with theft, and I was charged as his accomplice, having assisted him in his crime.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: It isn't really that bad... The missing wallets are all in the leftmost drawer of the Maison Gardiennage's big filing cabinet. We just need to see how long it takes to discover them.

dialogues.speaker: Lynette
dialogues.text: Yes, we should be released then.

dialogues.speaker: Lyney
dialogues.text: In terms of the magic trick itself, I think the performance went perfectly.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Leave it to Lyney to magic himself into prison.

choices.text: That's not the point, Lyney...

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Indeed. Last time I hid my identity from you, I promised that I'd tell you absolutely everything if you were angry about it, no more secrets.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: So I don't plan on keeping anything from you this time, either. At the moment, the House of the Hearth's interests don't conflict with yours at all.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: We were instructed by the "Father" of our House, The Knave, to come here and conduct an investigation.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Told you so! See, Paimon guessed right.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: As for what we're investigating... Perhaps you haven't heard, but the Fortress of Meropide hides a secret.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Some even say that the entire fortress exists just to protect it.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: The House of the Hearth has been investigating this for a very long time, trying to uncover its mysteries...

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: But recently all of our informants, including the ones that had infiltrated the guards, suddenly vanished and have not been heard from since.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: We believe that this is a direct provocation, and it's the reason why we came here.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Why is the House so interested about this secret?

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: "Father" has somehow managed to confirm that Focalors does not have Fontaine's Gnosis.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh!? How did she manage to learn information that important?

response.speaker: Lynette
response.text: "Father" has her ways... Many of them are beyond our imagination, and we've never had the chance to see her at work. But we trust her conclusions.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: It was this information that led us to suspect that Fontaine's Gnosis might be in the Fortress of Meropide, and is related to that "secret."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So it's all about the Gnosis again.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Well, that's about it from our side, how about you two? Did Monsieur Neuvillette send you here?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Bingo! The Knave has been applying a lot of pressure. She wants to know what happened to Childe, so we came here to investigate...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #...Ah! {NICKNAME}... Are we allowed to tell them?

choices.text: You've already said everything...

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Hehe, you don't need to worry too much about that. She's just asking for a report on Master Childe's predicament as a means of pressuring you.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: "Father" used the situation as a pretext to negotiate with two high-ranking officials in the Court of Fontaine. She actually just wants to be able to make concessions on this matter for gains elsewhere, almost like a bargaining chip.

response.speaker: Lynette
response.text: Sometimes, you need an excuse to do things you otherwise couldn't, and a Harbinger is more valuable than you might imagine.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Of course, it's not a complete farce. If we do manage to find out what happened to Master Childe too, then diplomatic relations with Fontaine could improve, and Snezhnaya might even be able to adjust its stance a bit.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Is it just Paimon, or does it feel like we're the only ones who actually care about Childe's situation... The relationships between the Harbingers must be as bad as ever.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: I wouldn't go that far... "Father" just has different standards than we do when it comes to what can be sacrificed for an advantage. By the way, I have a suggestion. Why don't we team up?

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Even though we have different objectives, we're both here to investigate the Fortress of Meropide. It would be more efficient for us to work together.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: As you know, the House of the Hearth has many reasons to seek the Gnosis, but our highest priority remains resolving the prophesized crisis. You can trust us on that.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Sorry, I must refuse.

response.speaker: Lynette
response.text: See? I told you.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Is that so... Sure enough, it won't be easy to convince them to cooperate with us...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Lyney seems to be thinking pretty hard about something...

response.speaker: Lynette
response.text: Of course he is! Lyney has been looking forward to a chance to reach an understanding with you ever since last we met.

response.speaker: Lynette
response.text: Or I should say, we were really looking forward to teaming up with you this time.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Lynette! Just tell them everything, why don't you...

response.speaker: Lynette
response.text: It's okay to open up a little...

choices.text: If all we're doing is sharing info... fine.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Very prudent of you, and consistent with your behavior since we first met. That's reasonable enough, and I agree to cooperate on these terms as well.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: I was prepared for the worst, but you were actually more agreeable than I anticipated. Alright then, there's no time to lose. I have some information to share, so listen carefully.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Since Lynette and I arrived here, our investigation uncovered the fact that the Fortress of Meropide has a "forbidden zone."

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Most people just clammed up and wouldn't talk, but after asking the right questions, we were able to confirm the existence of the forbidden zone from the guards.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: You should be aware of that while you're investigating.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A forbidden zone...? Could that be where Childe disappeared to? You're right, we'll definitely keep that in mind.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Good. That's the most suspicious thing about the fortress that we know of so far. We have a few other unanswered questions, and we'll be investigating those as quickly as we can. Anyway, I hope you find our information useful, at least.

response.speaker: Lyney
response.text: Oh, look at the time! You two must be hungry. You should go to the Coupon Cafeteria and get something to eat. I'll use my cards to get in touch with you again in the future.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's just what Paimon wanted to hear! Paimon's starving after all that work today! We can talk more about the investigation later, let's go get some grub!

choices.text: But I may reconsider if things get serious.
Consider it an exchange of information.
The question is, what are you two really doing here?

talks.objective: Go to the Coupon Cafeteria to get some food

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: He wasn't kidding. Today's meal is nowhere near as good as last time. *sigh* Who knows how long it'll be until we're lucky enough to get that super tasty meal again...

choices.text: As long as you're here long enough...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh, forget about it then. We'll just deal with the regular food for the time being. Let's just get out of here as soon as possible.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But life here doesn't seem all that bad, other than the foreman being kinda mean and the work being pretty tiring...

response.speaker: Vidoc
response.text: You think so, mate? Ah, if I had a coupon for every fish who's said that...

response.speaker: Vidoc
response.text: Seems you fishies still haven't learned your lessons from your life up on the surface...

response.speaker: Vidoc
response.text: If you take things at face value, then by the time you reach a dead end, you won't even know how you ended up on that road in the first place.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Have some advice for us, old timer?

response.speaker: Vidoc
response.text: Heh, I like your attitude. I can let you in on a little something...

response.speaker: Vidoc
response.text: Everyone's been telling you to just follow the rules and not cause any trouble for yourself, am I right?

response.speaker: Vidoc
response.text: But what they don't tell you is that the rules aren't exactly what they pretend to be — the rules for being a prisoner.

response.speaker: Vidoc
response.text: The truth is, this place has a lot of "hidden rules"...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? "Hidden rules"? ...What do you mean?

response.speaker: Vidoc
response.text: Not everyone knows about those rules, but whether you know 'em or not, once you break one... you might encounter something even worse than death.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: R—Really...? Ooh, now you're really scaring poor Paimon, don't joke around like that...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Have some advice for us, old timer?

response.speaker: Vidoc
response.text: Of course, and I'd say that just disappearing would be one of the better outcomes.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, you mean that if there really are "hidden rules," then Childe's disappearance might have something to do with that?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, in that case... Would you tell us some hidden rules? We definitely want to avoid breaking them...

response.speaker: Vidoc
response.text: Hehe... C'mon mate, this is valuable information, the difference between life and death. D'you really think you can just ask and I would tell you?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon understands... But we don't have many Credit Coupons yet...

response.speaker: Vidoc
response.text: Yeah, yeah, I know... Not like I'm going anywhere. Just come talk to me after you've saved enough.

response.speaker: Vidoc
response.text: Moreover, you're new fish, freshly caught, and completely out of your element... What'd be the point in even telling you anything before you've gotten a handle on your new lives? Come and find me once you've been here longer.

response.speaker: Vidoc
response.text: I'm usually around the Rag and Bone Shop. Just call me Vidoc. Bye bye now.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: He left, just like that? Do you think he's just trying to scare us into buying fake information from him?

choices.text: Is it possible that someone would just disappear?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, it might be a good place to start in our investigation. "Hidden rules," huh...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But like he said, we don't have any coupons, and we're still not very familiar with this place. There's nothing we can do about it now.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah! We were so busy talking, we almost forgot to eat! Even if it's not the best, it's probably better while it's warm. C'mon, dig in before it gets cold!

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: After your meal, you spend some time getting familiar with the fortress. Before long, it's nighttime...

choices.text: But I'm still interested.
It'll only be a matter of time before you get it again.

talks.objective: Return to the dormitories to rest

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, Paimon just confirmed with the guards that our shift is set for every morning, and we're free to do whatever we want all afternoon...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...But it seems like most of the other inmates choose to continue working through the afternoon to earn more Credit Coupons.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, and they also said that you can use coupons to skip work in the morning and free up your time.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: They weren't kidding... Credit Coupons really can be used to do anything here...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: *yawn* Paimon's so tired... and we'll need to wake up and go to work in the morning. Without any Credit Coupons, it's not like we can really do anything else.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Nighty night, {NICKNAME}. Paimon hopes we can keep making progress on our investigation tomorrow.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: "I hear... someone calling me..."

talks.objective: Additional

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So this is the actual entrance to the Fortress of Meropide.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It looks like there are other new arrivals, too. They sure don't look happy... Maybe we look too relaxed for fresh convicts?

choices.text: Hurry up and think about something sad.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, right... we're on someone else's territory now. We need to think of a good way to act like criminals to get by...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If we're discovered, even Neuvillette might not be able to rescue us...

choices.text: If we ever get found out...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: H—Hey, don't scare Paimon! Oooh, Paimon's not ready for all this...

response.speaker: Deakin
response.text: Uh, look, I don't really know you, and I have no idea what kind of crime you committed, but... You wouldn't have happened to anger someone important, did you?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... Someone important? Paimon... doesn't think so? Wait, why are you suddenly trying to talk to us now?

response.speaker: Deakin
response.text: Now's not the time to worry about that. Anyway, it's over there, so... you just go on over by yourselves. I've done my job, so... good luck!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What was that all about? Eh? Wait a second, are there usually so many Gardemeks around here?

choices.text: Apparently not...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Th—They're already on to us!?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Get ready to fight.
Prisoners number 7459 and 7560, welcome. No need to be anxious, these Gardemeks aren't here to attack you. In fact, they're here as your "honor guard."
When I heard that you were friends of Monsieur Neuvillette, I had the Gardemeks come and wait in formation.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, you know about our connection with Neuvillette?
The seafloor isn't as cut off from the world as you might imagine. However, I'm afraid that I know nothing more than that you are friends of the Iudex.
And as you can see, committing a crime means being sentenced here, even if you're friends with the Chief Justice. Quite fair.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So, you must be...

response.speaker: Deakin
response.text: Th—The Duke! Greetings, Your Grace! L—Lovely weather today, isn't it?

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: Greetings, my good fellow. I'm willing to imagine that the weather is as good outside the sea as you say it is. Ah, how great it would have been if only the Fortress of Meropide had been built on the coast. It would have been so convenient to enjoy a nice chat in the sunshine.

response.speaker: Deakin
response.text: Ah! My profuse apologies, I just got so nervous when I saw you, I just...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So this is the Duke... He sure looks a lot younger than Paimon imagined!

response.speaker: Wriothesley
response.text: #{NICKNAME} and Paimon, correct? Mr. Deakin here was responsible for your welcome. I trust you were satisfied with his guidance?

choices.text: Does this mean that...
Then maybe we'd become criminals for real.
You're probably the only one who doesn't fit in.

talks.objective: Additional

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So if the machine gets jammed, you just need to attack it to fix the problem!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Once the widget is hot enough to glow, jump to step on the pedal and hit the widget with the hammer!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay, you've got this!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Great, now we can report back to the foreman and give him the processed widgets!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Lyney! Mr. Magician! Where are you? This had better not be some disappearing act!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: He doesn't seem to be around here. Let's try looking somewhere else.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Where could he be? Did he decide to slack off and sleep the day away?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So we're going even deeper now? Just how deep down are we?

dialogues.speaker: Deakin
dialogues.text: It's like a metaphor for your previous life, isn't it?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... our lives weren't that bad!
